title: The Hare and the Hyena’s Bag
summary: The hare tricks a greedy hyena into carrying him home in a bag, and the road teaches the hyena a lesson about measuring a favour.
moral: The one who asks for the whole road ends up carrying the traveller.
attribution: A traditional Mandinka tale, retold for Ubuntu Tales.

cover.alt: A hare peering from a woven bag slung across a hyena’s back beneath a baobab

sentences.text: A hyena found a bag of grain beside the road and was deciding how to carry it home when the hare came along, walking as if he had all day.
“That is a heavy bag,” the hare said.
“Shall I help you carry it?
I am small, but I am clever about weight.”
The hyena did not like the word clever.
“I will carry it myself,” she said.
“And I will carry you too, if you keep talking, because you look lighter than the bag.”
The hare climbed in.
The hyena tied the bag shut and put it on her back, pleased with herself, and started up the road.
After a while the hare, inside the bag, began to complain that the grain was pressing into him.
“Put me on top,” he said.
“I will keep watch for thieves.”
The hyena opened the bag and put the hare on top of the grain.
The hare kept watch, and after a while he said, “There is a thief behind us.
Let me off, and I will chase him.”
The hyena let him off, and the hare ran off, and that was the last she saw of him for a while.
At the top of the road the hyena met the hare again, walking as if he had all day.
“You left me with the bag,” she growled.
“Yes,” said the hare.
“But I also kept the thieves away, and I carried the weight of the bag from the moment I sat on it.
You measured the favour wrong.”
The hyena went home with the grain and no answer, which is the worst way to end an argument.
The old people say she has been wary of small animals carrying bags ever since, and the hare still walks as if he has all day — which, somehow, he does.
